question: Rakesh sold 150 chairs and had a gain equal to the selling price of 75 chairs. What is his profit percentage?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the Selling Price (SP) of 1 chair be 1 unit.

Total SP = 150 units, Profit = SP of 75 chairs = 75 units.

Cost Price (CP) = Total SP − Profit = 150 − 75 = 75 units.

Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100 = (75 ÷ 75) × 100 = 100%.

**∴ The correct answer is 100%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number of chairs sold = 150

Gain = Selling Price (SP) of 75 chairs

**Formula Used:**

Gain = SP − Cost Price (CP)

Gain % = (Gain ÷ CP) × 100

 
 
• 
 
• 
 
• 
 Total SP of 150 chairs = 150 units

 
 
 CP = 75 units

 
 
 Profit = 75 units

 
 Profit % = (75 ÷ 75) × 100 = 100%

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let the Selling Price of 1 chair be 1 unit.

⇒ Total SP of 150 chairs = 150 × 1 = 150 units

⇒ Gain = SP of 75 chairs = 75 × 1 = 75 units

⇒ We know that CP = SP − Gain

⇒ CP of 150 chairs = 150 − 75 = 75 units

⇒ Substitute CP and Gain values into the formula to find Gain % :

⇒ Gain % = (75 ÷ 75) × 100

⇒ Gain % = 1 × 100 = 100%

**∴ The correct answer is 100%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit and Loss Basics

Profit occurs when Selling Price > Cost Price. Profit = SP − CP. Loss occurs when Cost Price > Selling Price. Loss = CP − SP.

Profit/Loss Percentage

Both profit and loss percentages are always calculated on the Cost Price (CP) as the base, unless the question explicitly specifies otherwise. Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100.

Dishonest Dealer Concept

When a dealer claims to sell goods at Cost Price but uses a false weight, the actual profit percentage is given by: Profit % = (True Weight − False Weight) ÷ False Weight × 100.
